title: New York salons and barbershops
hypothesis: Use the NY DOS establishment register to identify a named license holder at an active salon or barbershop. Treat an establishment or barbershop-owner holder as license-role owner evidence, a renter as an independent chair-business candidate rather than the shop owner, and an individual practitioner as neither. Only an explicitly published shop contact, independently linked to the same person in an owner/founder role, can advance to the normal authorized contact gates.
ownerSource: NY DOS Appearance Enhancement and Barber Business and Area Renter Licensees (`ny_salons` / `y3u4-jbgh`): DOSAEBUSINESS and DOSBARSHOPOWNER are parsed as Owner; DOSAERENTER and DOSBARRENTER are parsed as Suite Renter.
phoneSource: No phone is in the NY DOS register. The safe alternative is an explicitly published shop business contact that is independently linked to the named license holder; no residential lookup, property match, private-phone append, or inferred chair-renter handset is eligible.

workflow.label: Active NY DOS establishment row
workflow.detail: Read an in-scope `ny_salons` row with a future expiration, person-form license holder, business name, and shop address.

workflow.label: License-role decision
workflow.detail: Classify the four business and renter license types; an individual cosmetology or barber credential is outside this source and does not establish employment or ownership.

workflow.label: Employee or practitioner hold
workflow.detail: Do not use a practitioner-only record, stylist, or barber as the business owner merely because the person works at the address.

workflow.label: Establishment-holder candidate
workflow.detail: DOSAEBUSINESS and DOSBARSHOPOWNER identify the license holder for that establishment; preserve this as license-role evidence, not direct-phone proof.

workflow.label: Chair-renter candidate
workflow.detail: DOSAERENTER and DOSBARRENTER identify a renter's own service business candidate; never relabel the renter as the salon or suite-operator owner.

workflow.label: Published shop-contact check
workflow.detail: Use only a lawfully obtained, explicitly published business contact at the same shop; a shared reception, booking, or suite-operator number is a business-contact alternative, not a direct owner line.

workflow.label: Contact or role unresolved
workflow.detail: Hold when there is no public shop contact, the contact is shared, or independent owner/founder evidence does not link the holder or renter to that number.

workflow.label: Independent owner-role check
workflow.detail: Require current independent owner/founder evidence for the same business and an explicit direct-business-contact link. License-holder evidence alone does not prove handset ownership.

workflow.label: Authorized contact gates
workflow.detail: Only after role and public-contact support, evaluate line type, reachability, DNC/TCPA, suppression, and timezone under separately authorized processes.

workflow.label: Deliver after all gates
workflow.detail: No current NY salon/barber path has measured owner-contact outcomes or qualifies a private phone for delivery.

workflow.label: Private-address route blocked
workflow.detail: Do not parcel-match the business address or trace a residence to obtain a private phone for this industry.

failures.risk: A cosmetologist, stylist, or barber is treated as a shop owner because they work at the same address.
failures.mitigation: Keep the individual-license dataset outside this workflow and hold practitioner/employment-only records; require the establishment license role or independent owner/founder evidence.

failures.risk: A chair renter is presented as the owner of the salon, suite building, or operator.
failures.mitigation: Retain renter status as Suite Renter and only consider the renter's own independently evidenced business; do not promote the renter to shop owner.

failures.risk: The named license holder is assumed to own a mobile or to be reachable on a shared booking/reception number.
failures.mitigation: Treat every public number as a business-contact candidate until current independent owner/founder and explicit direct-contact evidence support the same person and normal contact gates pass.

failures.risk: Recipe B parcel matching and skip tracing turn a shop record into a residential/private-phone lookup.
failures.mitigation: Add an industry-specific pre-parcel hold for `salon_barber_ny`; do not call parcel or trace for these rows. Route only a published shop contact into an authorized future evaluation.

failures.risk: A suite or multi-chair address makes a shared operator line appear direct to every listed holder.
failures.mitigation: Hold shared or operator contacts and require a contact explicitly published for, and independently connected to, the individual business owner before delivery.

sources.label: NY DOS Appearance Enhancement and Barber Business and Area Renter Licensees
sources.scope: Active NY business, barbershop-owner, area-renter, and barber-renter rows; name, business, address, issue and expiration dates; no phone.

sources.label: NY DOS individual appearance enhancement licensees
sources.scope: Practitioner name pool without business address or ownership/employment role.

sources.label: Published shop business contact with independent owner/founder support
sources.scope: A future lawful business-contact route for a matched shop or renter business; no free verified endpoint is wired for this recipe.

iterations.hypothesis: The NY parser preserves the four materially different license roles without converting a business-name holder into a person.
iterations.test: Five-case local fixture/code audit of `tests/fixtures/registers/ny_salons.json` through `nySalons`, plus the focused test's synthetic renter and expired-row branches, on 2026-09-24.
iterations.observed: All five saved active fixture rows parsed as person-form DOSAEBUSINESS Owner rows with no phone. The focused assertions also classify DOSAERENTER as Suite Renter and hold an expired row. This is parser behavior only, not a live coverage or contact measurement.
iterations.change: Keep establishment-holder and renter labels distinct in the review; reject employee/practitioner inference and do not describe a license holder as owner-confirmed mobile.

iterations.hypothesis: The live recipe can use the register without private-address discovery.
iterations.test: Code audit of `pullNames`, `parcelStep`, and `traceStep` for the live recipe-B mapping on 2026-09-24.
iterations.observed: `salon_barber_ny` maps to `ny_salons` with recipe B. The runner stores the person as `owner_name`, then routes phoneless rows to parcel resolution and BatchData skip tracing; it has no public-shop-contact branch or owner-evidence hold.
iterations.change: Propose a pre-parcel hold for this industry and a future public-contact/owner-evidence route; no paid or private lookup was run.

measurement.result: Five saved active NY salon fixture rows parsed as person-form establishment holders with no phone; synthetic test branches classify a renter as Suite Renter and an expired row as held. No live source call, owner-contact, mobile, reachability, or DNC outcome was measured.

cost.basis: Local fixture and code audit only; no paid discovery, private-phone append, parcel lookup, trace, or phone verification was invoked.
cost.note: No cost per clean owner contact is measurable without separately authorized public-contact, owner-role, and contact-outcome observations.

implementation.summary: The live `ny_salons` adapter filters active in-scope license types, parses person holders, labels establishment holders as Owner and renters as Suite Renter, and retains no register phone. However, `salon_barber_ny` is live recipe B: the jobs service writes the holder to `owner_name` and directs phoneless rows to residential parcel matching and paid tracing. It does not implement a public-shop-contact branch, shared-line hold, or independent owner-evidence gate.

nextMeasurement: After the pre-parcel hold and a lawful public-shop-contact route are implemented, run a consented 5-20 row aggregate study that separately records active establishment holders, renters, practitioner holds, published shop contacts, shared contacts, independently supported owner contacts, and authorized line outcomes. Do not use residential/property data or private-phone appends.
